page: Microsoft Azure M128ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the MSMediumMemoryv2 family, virtualized on Microsoft Hyper-V. Built upon 64-bit x86 Intel processor architecture, the instance provides 128 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 3892.0 GB of system memory. This yields a high memory density of approximately 30.41 GB per core, positioning the server for environments requiring large working sets to reside continuously in system memory. The instance does not include integrated graphics processing units.

Storage architecture relies entirely on external disks, as the M128ms_v2 features no bundled local instance storage. It supports Azure Premium Storage for external disk volumes to handle operating system and database persistence. Networking configurations do not provision complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default, relying instead on configured virtual networks, private addressing, or dedicated public IP resources.

Given its massive memory capacity and dedicated compute allocation, the instance is targeted toward extreme memory-bound enterprise applications. It is suited for in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive relational database management systems, in-memory data analytics engines, and enterprise resource planning platforms where high memory capacity minimizes disk fetch latency.
description: Microsoft Azure M128ms_v2 is a dedicated memory-optimized virtual machine within the MSMediumMemoryv2 family, managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. Built upon 64-bit x86 Intel architecture, it provides 128 dedicated vCPUs and 3892.0 GB of RAM, translating to roughly 30.41 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring attached remote disks such as Premium Storage for persistent file and operating system volumes, and it does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its massive memory-to-vCPU allocation, the M128ms_v2 delivers high resource density for workloads requiring vast amounts of real-time in-memory data processing. It is engineered primarily for extreme enterprise database deployments, in-memory analytics systems, enterprise resource planning platforms such as SAP HANA, and large-scale transactional workloads that demand expansive RAM capacities.
